record.title: The CTI–ITC polynomial equality conjecture for complete split graphs
record.statement:
Let $S_{n,d}$ be the complete split graph, and let $\mathfrak{F}_{n,d}^{CTI}(q,t)$ and $\mathfrak{F}_{n,d}^{ITC}(q,t)$ denote the $q,t$-CTI and $q,t$-ITC polynomials, respectively. **CTI–ITC equality conjecture.**

$$
\mathfrak{F}_{n,d}^{CTI}(q,t)=\mathfrak{F}_{n,d}^{ITC}(q,t).
$$

Equality is known in some special cases, but the general case remains unresolved. It is equivalent, using the established equality of the $q,t$-Schröder and $q,t$-ITC polynomials, to the Schröder-polynomial formulation appearing below.
record.source_name: Henri Derycke, Mark Dukes and Yvan Le Borgne, “The sandpile model on the complete split graph: q,t-Schröder polynomials, sawtooth polyominoes, and a cycle lemma”, arXiv:2402.15372 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15372

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: The conjecture on negative oriented distinguishing index when the distinguishing index is two
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $D'(G)$ denote its distinguishing index and $OD'^-(G)$ its negative oriented distinguishing index.

**Conjecture for distinguishing index two.** If

$$
D'(G)=2,
$$

then

$$
OD'^-(G)=1.
$$

This is motivated by the preceding determination of the parameter for several graph classes and remains open. It concerns the values of the negative oriented distinguishing index for graphs whose distinguishing index equals two.
record.source_name: Aleksandra Gorzkowska and Jakub Kwaśny, “Arc-distinguishing of orientations of graphs”, arXiv:2402.16169 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.16169

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2024). “Another open question is about the values of $OD'^+$ and $OD'^-$ for balanced bipartite graphs, which have an automorphism that interchanges the bipartition sets.”

record.title: The critical bias ratio conjecture for the square lattice
record.statement:
Let $\rho(\mathbb{Z}^2)$ denote the critical bias ratio of the Maker–Breaker percolation game on the square lattice.

**Critical bias ratio conjecture.**

$$
\rho(\mathbb{Z}^2)=1.
$$

This is motivated by the heuristic that Maker claims a proportion $1/(1+\rho)$ of the edges and therefore behaves like bond percolation with parameter $p=1/(1+\rho)$; since $p_{\operatorname{c}}(\mathbb{Z}^2)=1/2$, the threshold should occur at $\rho=1$.
record.source_name: Vojtěch Dvořák, Adva Mond and Victor Souza, “The Maker-Breaker percolation game on a random board”, arXiv:2402.17547 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17547

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2024).

record.title: The critical bias ratio conjecture for vertex-transitive graphs
record.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a connected vertex-transitive graph. Write $p_{\operatorname{c}}(\Lambda)$ for its bond percolation threshold, and let $\rho(\Lambda)$ denote the critical bias ratio of the Maker–Breaker percolation game on $\Lambda$.

**Critical bias ratio conjecture.** If $\Lambda$ is a connected vertex-transitive graph, then

$$
\rho(\Lambda)=\frac{1}{p_{\operatorname{c}}(\Lambda)}-1.
$$

The formula extends the heuristic for $\mathbb{Z}^2$: under random-like play, Maker's claimed edges should resemble bond percolation with parameter $1/(1+\rho)$, so the game threshold should coincide with the percolation threshold. Its validity for general connected vertex-transitive graphs remains open.
record.source_name: Vojtěch Dvořák, Adva Mond and Victor Souza, “The Maker-Breaker percolation game on a random board”, arXiv:2402.17547 (2024).

record.title: Characterization of spherical orbit spaces from affine colorings
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a simple $n$-polytope, let $\boldsymbol\lambda$ be an affine coloring of $P$ of rank $r$, and let $\mathcal{C}(P,\lambda)$ and $\mathcal{C}(n,r+1)$ denote the associated complexes. Let $N(P,\lambda)$ be the space corresponding to this affine coloring.

**Spherical orbit-space conjecture.** The space $N(P,\lambda)$ is homeomorphic to $S^n$ if and only if

$$
\mathcal{C}(P,\lambda)\simeq\mathcal{C}(n,r+1).
$$

The claim gives a combinatorial characterization of when the orbit space associated with an affine coloring is an $n$-sphere. The supplied text does not indicate whether this statement has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Nikolai Erokhovets, “Manifolds realized as orbit spaces of non-free Z_2^k-actions on real moment-angle manifolds”, arXiv:2403.00492 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.00492

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Negative curvature from nonpositive factors in Cartesian graph products
record.statement:
Let $G^{(1)}$ and $G^{(2)}$ be graphs. For vertices indexed by $i$ and $j$, let ${\boldsymbol p}_i^{(1)}$ and ${\boldsymbol p}_j^{(2)}$ denote their node resistance curvatures, and let ${\boldsymbol p}_{i\otimes j}$ denote the node resistance curvature at the corresponding vertex of the Cartesian product. **Cartesian-product negativity conjecture.** If

$$
{\boldsymbol p}_i^{(1)},{\boldsymbol p}_j^{(2)}\le 0,
$$

then

$$
{\boldsymbol p}_{i\otimes j}<0.
$$

This is presented as the most general conjectured implication for Cartesian graph products and is intended to capture the emergence of negative curvature at product vertices whose two factor curvatures are nonpositive. Its resolution is not indicated in the source.
record.source_name: Aleyah Dawkins, Vishal Gupta, Mark Kempton, William Linz, Jeremy Quail, Harry Richman and Zachary Stier, “Node resistance curvature in Cartesian graph products”, arXiv:2403.01037 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01037

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Factorial-partition congruence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $M=(j)_{j=1}^{\infty}$, let $p_M(n)$ denote the number of partitions into the corresponding factorial parts, and define

$$
D_r=\prod_{p\leq r-2}p^{\left\lfloor\frac{r-2}{p}\right\rfloor}.
$$

Let $\sigma$ be the sum defined in the preceding $M$-ary partition conjecture, and let $c\in\{1,2\}$. Then

**Factorial-partition congruence conjecture.**

$$
p_M(r!n-\sigma-c)\equiv0\pmod{r!/D_r}.
$$

This is presented as a specialization of the preceding $M$-ary partition congruence conjecture. The supplied text does not report a resolution.
record.source_name: Błażej Żmija, “High order congruences for M-ary partitions”, arXiv:2403.04495 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04495

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: PSPACE-completeness conjecture for sums of superstars
record.statement: Let a sum of superstars be a disjunctive sum of impartial combinatorial games whose components are superstars, and let \ruleset{Paint Can} denote the corresponding game. **PSPACE-completeness conjecture.** A sum of superstars, and hence \ruleset{Paint Can}, is \cclass{PSPACE}-complete. The sum of superstars is already known to be \cclass{NP}-hard, while its precise complexity remains open; it is known to be solvable in polynomial space in the number of bits representing the sum.
record.source_name: Kyle Burke, Matthew Ferland, Svenja Huntemann and Shang-Hua Teng, “A Tractability Gap Beyond Nim-Sums: It's Hard to Tell Whether a Bunch of Superstars Are Losers”, arXiv:2403.04955 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.04955

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: The cyclic sieving conjecture for decorated permutations and extended codes
record.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $C_n$ be the cyclic group, let $\widetilde{{\mathfrak S}}_{n,j-1}$ be the set of decorated permutations with the specified excedance statistic, and let $\widetilde a_{n,j}(q)$ be the associated polynomial.

**Cyclic sieving conjecture.** For any positive integer $n$ and $0\leq j\leq n$, the triple

$$
\left(\widetilde{{\mathfrak S}}_{n,j-1},~C_n,~\widetilde a_{n,j}(q)\right)
$$

exhibits the cyclic sieving phenomenon.

The conjecture is motivated by the anticipated $C_n$-equivariant bijection between decorated permutations and extended Stembridge codes. The supplied text gives no resolution evidence, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Hsin-Chieh Liao, “Stembridge codes, permutahedral varieties, and their extensions”, arXiv:2403.10577 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10577

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2024). “This link to geometry was proved by Brosnan and Chow and Guay-Paquet .”

record.title: The perfect-game existence conjecture for PackIt! grids
record.statement:
Let $m \leq n$ be positive integers. Write $P(m,n)$ for the set of primes relevant to the $m \times n$ grid, let $\gamma(m,n)$ denote its gap, and let $K(m,n)$ be the total number of turns in a perfect game; write $\mathbf{1}_{K_p}$ for the indicator that $K(m,n)+1$ is prime. **Perfect-game existence conjecture.** If

$$
|P(m,n)| \leq \gamma(m,n) \leq K(m,n)-|P(m,n)|-\mathbf{1}_{K_p},
$$

then it is possible to complete a perfect game of PackIt! for the $m \times n$ grid. The preceding bounds show that this is precisely a range in which perfect packings are not ruled out a priori; the authors report no counterexamples in this range, but the assertion remains unproved.
record.source_name: Thomas Garrison, Marijn J. H. Heule and Bernardo Subercaseaux, “PackIt! Gamified Rectangle Packing”, arXiv:2403.12195 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12195

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).

record.title: Density of possible pentagon centers outside a disk
record.statement: Let $P_0$ be the original pentagon in the Eden model, and let $u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4,u_5$ be the five possible translation vectors between centers of neighboring pentagons. The set of possible centers is generated subject to the non-overlapping constraint of the model. **Density conjecture.** The set of possible centers of pentagons in the model is dense outside a disk around the origin. The claim concerns how the irrational relations among the translation vectors interact with the geometric non-overlap constraint; the source gives no further result establishing or disproving this density.
record.source_name: Claudia Silva, Erika Roldan and Rosemberg Toala-Enriquez, “Eden model for Pentagons”, arXiv:2403.12772 (2024).

record.title: Butler et al.'s complement coalescing conjecture for distance matrices
record.statement: Let $G_1$ and $G_2$ be graphs with $B_1\subseteq V(G_1)$ and $B_2\subseteq V(G_2)$. **Coalescing conjecture.** If coalescing the same connected rooted graph onto every vertex of $B_1$ and $B_2$ always produces cospectral pairs for the distance matrix, then coalescing the same connected rooted graph onto every vertex of $V(G_1)\setminus B_1$ and $V(G_2)\setminus B_2$ should also always produce cospectral pairs for the distance matrix. This conjecture concerns whether a universal coalescing construction for specified vertex sets is preserved when those sets are replaced by their complements; the paper states that it answers the conjecture negatively.
record.source_name: Sajid Bin Mahamud, Steve Butler, Hannah Graff, Nick Layman, Taylor Luck, Jiah Jin, Noah Owen and Angela Yuan, “Coalescing sets preserving cospectrality of graphs arising from block similarity matrices”, arXiv:2404.01561 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01561

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of April 2024); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: The Stanley–Stembridge conjecture for chromatic symmetric functions
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a finite partially ordered set, and let $G$ be its incomparability graph. For a proper coloring of $G$, the associated chromatic symmetric function is $X_G$. A symmetric function is **$e$-positive** if its expansion in the basis of elementary symmetric functions has nonnegative coefficients.

**Stanley–Stembridge conjecture.** If $P$ is a ${\bf 3}+{\bf 1}$-avoiding partial order, then $X_G$ is $e$-positive.

The conjecture was reduced to natural unit interval orders by Guay-Paquet and was proved by Brosnan and Chow, independently of Guay-Paquet. The paper studies and reproves the special case for unit interval orders additionally avoiding ${\bf 2}+{\bf 1}+{\bf 1}$, originally due to Gebhard and Sagan.
record.source_name: Joseph McDonough, Pavlo Pylyavskyy and Shiyun Wang, “The Stanley-Stembridge Conjecture for 2 + 1 +1-avoiding unit interval orders: a diagrammatic proof”, arXiv:2404.07280 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.07280

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2024). “Shareshian-Wachs' conjecture was proved by Brosnan and Chow , and independently by Guay-Paquet .”

record.title: The Small Quasikernel Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a finite digraph. A **quasikernel** is an independent set $Q\subseteq V(D)$ such that every vertex $x\in V(D)$ satisfies $\operatorname{dist}(Q,x)\le 2$. The digraph $D$ is **source-free** if it has no vertex of in-degree $0$.

**Small Quasikernel Conjecture.** If $D$ is a source-free digraph, then $D$ contains a quasikernel $Q$ with

$$
|Q|\le\frac{1}{2}|V(D)|.
$$

This conjecture, due to P. L. Erdős and Székely, asks for a sharp universal upper bound on the size of a quasikernel in source-free digraphs. It is presented here as an open problem.
record.source_name: Sam Spiro, “Generalized Quasikernels in Digraphs”, arXiv:2404.07305 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.07305

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: The subexponential bound conjecture for disjoint q-kernels
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a finite digraph. A **source set** is a set of vertices with no in-neighbor outside the set, and $r$-disjoint $q$-kernels are $r$ pairwise disjoint sets that are each independent and reach every vertex by directed paths of length at most $q$.

**Subexponential disjoint q-kernel conjecture.** There exist constants $\varepsilon>0$ and $r_0$ such that, whenever $r\ge r_0$ and $D$ contains no $(r-1)$-source sets, $D$ contains $r$-disjoint $q$-kernels with

$$
q\le(2-\varepsilon)^r.
$$

The conjecture would improve the paper's known exponential bound, whose growth rate is approximately $2^r$. The source identifies substantial barriers to proving it.
record.source_name: Sam Spiro, “Generalized Quasikernels in Digraphs”, arXiv:2404.07305 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.07305

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: Dominant-coefficient conjecture for the universal Drinfeld–Yetter algebra
record.statement: Let $c_{n,m}$ denote the coefficient introduced in Proposition, and let $r_n^\mathsf{id}$ and $r_m^\mathsf{id}$ be the corresponding elements of the universal Drinfeld–Yetter algebra. **Dominant-coefficient conjecture.** The coefficient $c_{n,m}$ is the dominant term of $r_n^\mathsf{id} \circ r_m^\mathsf{id}$, meaning that it is the term with greatest absolute value. This conjecture concerns the leading term in products in the universal Drinfeld–Yetter algebra; the supplied text gives no evidence of a proof or disproof.
record.source_name: Andrea Rivezzi, “On the universal Drinfeld-Yetter algebra”, arXiv:2404.16786 (2024).

record.title: The polynomial semiring sum-product partition conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{N}[x]$ be the polynomial semiring with coefficients in $\mathbb{N}$, and let $\mathbb{N}[x]=C_0\cup C_1$ be a bipartition. **The polynomial semiring conjecture.** There exist $i\in\{0,1\}$ and $f,g\in\mathbb{N}[x]$ such that

$$
\{f,g,f+g,fg\}\subseteq C_i.
$$

This asks for a monochromatic additive-multiplicative configuration in the polynomial semiring, where the paper identifies $\mathbb{N}[x]$ as an example not covered by its preceding subsemiring method; the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: T. Y. Tao and Neil N. Y. Yang, “Finding Product and Sum Patterns in non-commutative settings”, arXiv:2404.19650 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.19650

record.title: Dong's vertex-isolation conjecture for mean color numbers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $w$ be a vertex of $G$. Write $G-w$ for the graph obtained by deleting $w$, and let $K_1$ be the one-vertex graph. **Dong's vertex-isolation conjecture.** One has

$$
\mu(G)\geq\mu((G-w)\cup K_1).
$$

This conjecture concerns whether isolating a vertex cannot increase the mean color number. Dong proved the related Bartels–Welsh lower-bound conjecture, but the supplied text gives no resolution status for this assertion.
record.source_name: Wushuang Zhai and Yan Yang, “Counterexamples to two conjectures on mean color numbers of graphs”, arXiv:2405.01890 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.01890

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2024).

record.title: Dong's one-edge-at-a-vertex conjecture for mean color numbers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $w$ be a vertex of $G$ with $d(w)\geq 1$, and let $H$ be obtained from $G$ by deleting all but one of the edges incident to $w$. **Dong's one-edge-at-a-vertex conjecture.** One has

$$
\mu(G)\geq\mu(H).
$$

This is a proposed monotonicity principle for the mean color number under deletion of edges incident to one vertex. The supplied text gives no resolution status for this conjecture.
record.source_name: Wushuang Zhai and Yan Yang, “Counterexamples to two conjectures on mean color numbers of graphs”, arXiv:2405.01890 (2024).

record.title: Conjecture that regular Bonnet-Myers sharp graphs are self-centered
record.statement: Let $G$ be a regular Bonnet-Myers sharp graph, and suppose the classification theorem for Bonnet-Myers sharp graphs assumes that $G$ is self-centered. **Regular-graph conjecture.** For regular graphs, the self-centeredness condition in the classification theorem can be dropped. This would extend the classification of regular Bonnet-Myers sharp graphs beyond the self-centered case; the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
